question: In 1966 Samuelson joked that stock markets had predicted nine of the last five recessions. When markets fell, what percent preceded recessions?
move: A signal that catches every case may still cry wolf half the time.
ask: How often do my worries come true, compared with how often I have them?
trap: Hearing that the market caught every recession and trusting each alarm.
hint: Count the alarms, then how many of them turned out real.
steps: Share of alarms that were right: 5 ÷ 9 ≈ 0.56
reference: Paul Samuelson, Science and Stocks, Newsweek, 19 September 1966
